title: A Vector for the Echo
premise: Yara Oyelaran navigates the Meridian Loop, a cargo run between two estranged human colonies, carrying not just freight but the cryogenic backups of her dead crewmates—copies she was ordered to destroy and never did. When a manifest anomaly reveals her mother's name aboard the Halcyon, a ship that officially never flew, Yara learns the 'last transmission' from Earth is actually a countdown: when it ends, both colonies' fleets will fire on each other, believing the other side launched first. The lie holding them apart was authored by her mother, who faked her own death to keep the peace—and now needs Yara to perpetuate it. In the end, Yara broadcasts the truth along with the echo of Earth's final message, choosing love and honesty over inherited duty, and the fleets stand down as the loop finally goes silent.
about_author: Vesper Montrose is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade relaying messages between ships that rarely spoke to one another. Their fiction explores what survives when institutions fail but signals do not.

chapters.title: The Long Quiet
chapters.summary: Yara pilots the Meridian Loop's final leg, listening to Earth's fading transmission loop while avoiding the hold where her crewmates' backups sleep. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as routine; she has made invisibility an art form, and we feel how much it costs her.

chapters.title: A Name That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Customs AI flags an impossible entry: Adeyemi Oyelaran listed on the Halcyon, a vessel stricken from every registry. Yara pulls the record in secret. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: grief cracked open—her mother died twelve years ago, or so the funeral said.

chapters.title: Cargo of the Sleeping
chapters.summary: Yara descends into the hold and confronts the backups she was ordered to incinerate, speaking aloud for the first time about why she kept them. POV: Yara with interlaced memory. Emotional beat: guilt transmuted into tenderness; loyalty revealed as her defining flaw and gift.

chapters.title: The Harbor Master's Offer
chapters.summary: Fleet liaison Davor Kess intercepts Yara at port, offering immunity if she surrenders the Halcyon's coordinates—he suspects the ship exists and wants it found before the colonies do. POV: alternating Yara/Davor. Emotional beat: the trap of being seen; duty wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Ghost Frequency
chapters.summary: Following a corrupted beacon, Yara finds the Halcyon adrift in a debris field—crewed by backups, including one bearing her mother's memories. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: uncanny reunion; love confronting its own imperfect copy.

chapters.title: What Mother Built
chapters.summary: The mother-backup explains the deception: Earth's last transmission is a forged war order on a timer, designed to force the colonies into unity through shared enemy fear—but it will kill instead. POV: mother/Adeyemi. Emotional beat: inheritance as burden; admiration curdling into fury.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Both colonial fleets mobilize as the countdown accelerates; Kess demands Yara let the lie run, arguing truth means mutual annihilation. POV: Davor, then Yara. Emotional beat: the theme crystallized—loyalty to people versus loyalty to truth, with no clean side.

chapters.title: The Hold Decides
chapters.summary: The sleeping backups vote—awakened briefly—to authorize Yara to broadcast everything, including their existence, accepting erasure as the price. POV: ensemble via Yara. Emotional beat: collective sacrifice; the dead choosing honesty over survival.

chapters.title: Last Transmission Loop
chapters.summary: Climax: Yara hijacks the relay network during the final minutes, broadcasting the forgery, the Halcyon's logs, and Earth's true last words—a lullaby—as both fleets hold fire triggers. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: terror and clarity fused; one voice against two armadas.

chapters.title: Echo, Answered
chapters.summary: The fleets stand down; the colonies open negotiations using the loop's silence as common ground. Yara releases the backups to wake or rest as they choose, then plots a new route between worlds that speak again. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: resolution without absolution—truth cost everything except the future.
